title: Ideal-product projection along affine maps of algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $f:Y\to X$ be affine, meaning representable with affine scheme base changes. Let $F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module and $I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent ideal. Modules and quasi-coherence are on the small etale ringed site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Let $J=(f^{-1}I)F\subseteq F$ be the submodule generated by local products via $f^{-1}\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_Y$. Equivalently $J$ is the image of $f^*I\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}F\to F$. Then $J$ is quasi-coherent and, as quasi-coherent submodules of $f_*F$, one has $$I(f_*F)=f_*J.$$ Here the left side is the submodule generated by products of local sections of $I$ and $f_*F$; direct image is for the induced morphism of ringed small etale topoi.

source.place: Tag 0GF8, lemma-affine-morphism-projection-ideal, statement and notation paragraph.

proof.text: Choose a jointly surjective family of affine etale scheme charts $u_i:U_i\to X$, by taking affine open covers of an atlas in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Put $V_i=Y\times_XU_i$, with projections $v_i:V_i\to Y$ and $f_i:V_i\to U_i$. By the assumed definition of affineness, $V_i$ is an affine scheme and $f_i$ is affine. The maps $v_i$ form an etale cover by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Write $I_i=I|_{U_i}$ and $F_i=F|_{V_i}$. Restriction preserves their local free presentations, hence their quasi-coherence [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module].

source.place: Tag 0GF8, lemma-affine-morphism-projection-ideal, proof: etale localization and reduction to Tag 01YP.

proof.text: For each scheme $T=U_i,V_i$, write $A_T$ for the equivalence [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. Let $I_i^Z,F_i^Z$ be the Zariski quasi-coherent modules corresponding to $I_i,F_i$. The inclusion $I_i\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_{U_i}$ restricts on opens to an ideal inclusion, so $I_i^Z$ is a quasi-coherent ideal. Scheme pullback and tensor product preserve quasi-coherence by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent] and [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections]. The multiplication map $f_i^*I_i^Z\otimes F_i^Z\to F_i^Z$ therefore has quasi-coherent image $J_i^Z$, and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-ideal-product] gives $I_i^Z(f_{i,*}F_i^Z)=f_{i,*}J_i^Z$. Also $f_{i,*}F_i^Z$ and $f_{i,*}J_i^Z$ are quasi-coherent: $f_i$ is quasi-compact separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], so the direct-image clause of the equivalence applies.

source.place: Tag 0GF8, lemma-affine-morphism-projection-ideal, proof: etale localization and reduction to Tag 01YP.

proof.text: Transfer this equality to the small etale sites. The equivalence identifies scheme pullback and direct image with their etale versions. Its forward functor is tensor pullback; [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] identifies its tensor products. On a pure local tensor the resulting multiplication map sends $a\otimes s$ to the product of the pulled-back $a$ with $s$, because all these comparisons use the structural ring map. By [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison], $A_T$ is exact into the ambient etale module category: applying it to the quasi-coherent kernel-image and image-cokernel exact sequences carries the image inclusion to the ambient image inclusion. Their terms are quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] and [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel]. Thus $A_{V_i}J_i^Z=\operatorname{Im}(f_i^*I_i\otimes F_i\to F_i)$ and $I_i(f_{i,*}F_i)=f_{i,*}(A_{V_i}J_i^Z)$ as submodules, with every inclusion identified.

source.place: Tag 0GF8, lemma-affine-morphism-projection-ideal, proof: etale localization and reduction to Tag 01YP.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction], $(f_*F)|_{U_i}=f_{i,*}F_i$ and $(f_*J)|_{U_i}=f_{i,*}(J|_{V_i})$, compatibly with inclusions and scalars; also $(f^*I)|_{V_i}=f_i^*I_i$. Restricting a locally generated product submodule gives the product of the restrictions: its sections are precisely the sections which locally are finite sums of products, and the same etale refinements define both sides. Equivalently localization of a site retains the same covering families and hence the same local-image condition. It follows that $J|_{V_i}=A_{V_i}J_i^Z$ and $(I(f_*F))|_{U_i}=I_i(f_{i,*}F_i)$. Thus step 3 proves the desired equality on every $U_i$.

source.place: Tag 0GF8, lemma-affine-morphism-projection-ideal, proof: etale localization and reduction to Tag 01YP.

proof.text: The quasi-coherent local models $A_{V_i}J_i^Z$ show that $J$ is quasi-coherent: their free presentations, followed by the etale cover $\{V_i\to Y\}$, are presentations of $J$ locally on its site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Likewise $f_*F$ and the common submodule in step 4 are quasi-coherent, since on each $U_i$ they are the associated sheaves of the Zariski quasi-coherent modules in step 2. Finally equality of submodule sheaves is local: for a section of either submodule, pull back to the cover by the $U_i$; it lies in the other submodule there by step 4, and the sheaf gluing axiom puts it in that submodule before pullback. This gives both inclusions $I(f_*F)=f_*J$.
